short: A Wallachian prince whose terror tactics held off Mehmed II and outlived him in fiction.
full:
Vlad III of Wallachia, son of Vlad Dracul, held his principality three times; the reign that counts ran from 1456 to 1462. Wallachia lay between Hungary and an expanding Ottoman Empire, and Vlad had spent years as an Ottoman hostage. He centralised power by killing rival boyars, and in 1461 stopped paying tribute to Mehmed II and raided across the Danube through the winter.

Mehmed invaded in 1462 with a large army. Vlad refused battle, burned crops and poisoned wells, and mounted a night attack on the Ottoman camp; the campaign's lasting image is the field of impaled prisoners left outside Targoviste. Deposed in favour of his brother Radu, he was held in Hungary for years, returned briefly in 1476 and was killed within months. German pamphlets circulated accounts of his cruelty across Europe, and the patronymic Dracula was borrowed by Bram Stoker for a novel in 1897 that has almost buried the historical man. Sabaton's "Impaler", from Legends (2025), is about him.
